descriptionPlain:

A successful candidate will bring an outcome-oriented skillset to recombinant protein quantification and characterization. You will work collaboratively with our teams to produce and purify diverse proteins from cell culture processes and be comfortable conducting a wide range of protein quality assessments. This role will be based on-site in Emeryville, CA.

lists.content:
• Collaborate with cell line development and bioprocess teams for delivery of key internal technology programs and external customer projects. 
  • Develop, optimize, and validate assays for protein titer and quality for broad classes of recombinant therapeutic proteins. 
  • Plan and execute experimentation to understand protein quality through cell line, upstream and downstream process development.
  • Execute, summarize, interpret, and present routine and complex therapeutic protein characterizations.
  • Qualify and validate analytical procedures to compliance standards, upholding rigorous standards for execution and documentation.
  • Routinely operate, maintain, and troubleshoot analytical instrumentation (HPLCs, FPLCs, mass spectrometers).
  • Author, review, and implement methods, protocols, validations, and standard operating procedures. Ensure processes are followed in accordance with these standards.

• Hold a PhD in Analytical Chemistry, Molecular Biology, Biochemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, with 1+ years of biologics industry experience. Candidates without a PhD but with similar industry experience are encouraged to apply. 
  • Have illustrated experience in therapeutic protein characterization approaches (eg. HPLC, SDS, CE, cIEF, LC-MS). 
  • Have illustrated the ability to develop, execute, and interpret intact mass, sequence confirmation, and PTM analysis (e.g., glycosylation, disulfide mapping, peptide mapping) through mass spectrometry. 
  • Have illustrated the ability to develop, execute, and interpret aggregation and charge variant characterizations for biologics. 
  • Have experience in the development and execution of GLP-compliant methods characterizing protein quality attributes across a wide range of therapeutic classes.
  • Have hands-on experience operating LC-MS. Experience with Agilent QTOF instrumentation applied to assay protein quality is a plus, including familiarity with proteomic software. 
  • Are highly motivated to deliver successful outcomes for internal and external clients.
  • Are excited to work with internal and external clients to deliver project excellence.
    Have strong communication skills and are comfortable teaching and sharing knowledge at multiple levels of technical detail.

description:
Prolific Machines is ushering in a new era of biotechnology with light. Our first-of-its-kind optogenetic platform delivers unprecedented control, precisely guiding cellular behavior when and where it matters most. Unlike existing tools used to control biology, our technology enables dynamic, tunable control over virtually any cellular function in any cell type. We're enabling partners to unlock robust efficiency, quality, and reproducibility advantages across the most complex pharmaceuticals and therapeutic proteins. Prolific is supported by leading investors, including Bill Gates’s Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Mayfield and SOSV.


We're looking for a senior hardware leader to own the hardware engineering function at Prolific: the team that designs and builds our illumination systems, the hardware that delivers light to cells from the bench to bioreactor scale. Reporting to our Co-Founder and CTO, you will lead the transition from validated prototypes to robust, customer-grade products. You'll be the voice of hardware in company planning and be a key partner to the CTO in shaping Prolific's technical direction.

This is not a blank-slate role. You will inherit an exceptional, multidisciplinary team spanning mechatronics, optical, electrical, and firmware engineering that has already designed, built, and shipped illuminators into our own biology and bioprocess labs. They are highly skilled for their level of seniority, and the team has a culture we are genuinely proud of: collaborative, candid, and committed to doing excellent work. 

One discipline the team doesn't yet have is systems engineering, and we'd love you to bring it. That means architecting how our systems fit together: modular subsystems, clean interfaces, testable units, and components that are reused where it makes sense, all without over-engineering from the start. A systems engineering background is not strictly required, but a strong systems-level approach to hardware is central to this role.

At Prolific, hardware is an enabler rather than the product itself, working with partners over long trajectories. That makes it essential to be careful where rigor matters, and knowing the difference. 

As of today, Prolific is R&D-first: most of our hardware runs in our own labs and in early partner programs, not yet in large deployed fleets. But the timeline to customer-facing hardware is ambitious. The right person is energized by an R&D environment now and has done the R&D-to-product transition before, so they can lead the team through it rather than learn it along the way.

You don't need to be a biologist. Our scientists and bioprocess engineers work side by side with the hardware team, and you'll have deep biology expertise around you from day one. What we need from you is hardware leadership, strong communication and great curiosity.

In your first 6 to 12 months, you will:

  • Get to know the team and take over day-to-day leadership in a way that preserves what already works well, while setting a clear operating rhythm for planning, design reviews, and delivery
  • Own the roadmap for our next-generation illuminator platform, including oversight of external development partners
  • Define the path to GMP readiness for systems used in partner manufacturing environments
  • Set strong standards for documentation, communication and other good engineering practices
  • Shape the team's growth: identify the gaps, write the hiring plan, and make the first hires

Hardware operations and project management have dedicated owners on the team. You'll work closely with them, but you won't be running the shop by yourself.

This role is based on-site in Emeryville, CA, with the flexibility to work remotely on occasion.

lists.content:
Strategy and functional leadership

  • Translate company strategy into a multi-year hardware strategy and roadmap, and turn it into concrete functional plans, milestones, and success measures
  • Partner with the CTO to define Prolific's technical roadmap, engineering standards, and decision-making frameworks
  • Contribute to company business planning as the hardware function's representative, including budgets, headcount, capital equipment, and partner program commitments
  • Make most operational and technical decisions for the hardware function independently, escalating where strategic alignment is needed
  • Build strong partnerships with peer leaders in bioprocess engineering, biology, software, data, and business development so hardware plans integrate with company-wide priorities
  • Represent Prolific externally with partners, suppliers, and the broader engineering community, and bring outside expertise and industry connections into the company
  • Model commitment to company decisions, aligning the hardware team behind agreed outcomes even when they differ from your own recommendation

    • Leadership and team development

  • Conserve and strengthen the hardware team's culture of collaboration, candor, and craftsmanship as the team grows
  • Lead, mentor, and develop a strong multidisciplinary team, elevating already capable engineers to the next level and growing senior individual contributors into technical and people leads
  • Coach the team in balancing speed and rigor: when to prototype quickly, when to slow down and do it properly, and how to make that call with confidence
  • Own the structure and operations of the hardware function: team design, roles, resourcing, and a predictable operating rhythm (planning, design reviews, retrospectives) that adds clarity without adding bureaucracy
  • Own hardware team growth: identify capability gaps (e.g. systems, testing, quality), write the hiring plan, and hire people who strengthen the culture
  • Manage up and down effectively, communicating clearly about tradeoffs in scope, quality, time, and people

    • Hardware development

  • Bring a systems engineering approach to the platform: define subsystem boundaries and interfaces, requirements flow-down, and modular designs that enable rapid scaling, independent testing, and component reuse, without over-engineering early
  • Take on the hardest, least precedented technical problems in scaling light delivery to industrial bioprocessing, and develop solutions that hold up long term
  • Oversee the full development lifecycle, from technical scoping and concept through prototyping, verification and validation, and transfer to production
  • Lead the transition from R&D prototypes to reliable, serviceable, manufacturable products (design for manufacturing, design for service, design controls)
  • Drive make-vs-buy and insource-vs-outsource decisions, and manage external development partners and contract manufacturers against clear scopes and milestones
  • Support business development with technical scoping and realistic estimates for partner programs

    • Quality, compliance, and productization

  • Define and execute the path to GMP readiness for hardware used in partner manufacturing environments
  • Lead electrical safety and regulatory certification efforts with test labs and consultants
  • Establish the right-sized quality practices for each stage: documentation, change control, verification records, and supplier qualification
  • Work with hardware operations to make sure what the team designs can be built, deployed, and supported at scale

• BS, MS, or PhD in Mechanical, Electrical, Optical, Systems, or Biomedical Engineering, or a related field; equivalent experience considered
  • 10+ years of relevant industry experience, including 3+ years leading a multidisciplinary hardware engineering team or department as a people manager (e.g. senior manager or director)
  • Demonstrated experience taking at least one hardware product from R&D prototype through to production and field deployment, with concrete examples of what you'd do differently next time
  • A track record of setting multi-year technical or functional strategy and translating it into execution plans, budgets, and resourcing
  • Hands-on experience bringing hardware into a regulated environment: GMP, FDA design controls, or equivalent, and leading products through electrical safety certification (UL, CE, or similar)
  • Deep technical expertise in at least one core discipline (mechanical, electrical, or optical) and enough breadth to make sound architecture calls across the others
  • A strong track record of mentoring engineers and growing individual contributors into leads
  • Experience managing external development partners, contract manufacturers, or suppliers against defined scopes and milestones
  • Excellent written and verbal communication, including explaining complex technical tradeoffs in scope, quality, time, and (human) resources to executives, partners, and non-engineers

• Strong systems engineering judgment: enough depth in the discipline to decide whether we need a dedicated systems engineer and to lead that work until we do, whether or not it's your formal background. A track record of architecting modular, scalable hardware platforms is a strong signal here
  • Familiarity with life science hardware: bioprocessing equipment, lab instrumentation, or medical devices (biology expertise is available within the organization)
  • Experience with optical systems, LED or laser illumination, or thermal management of high-power electronics
  • Experience with equipment used in pharmaceutical manufacturing, including qualification (IQ/OQ/PQ) and GAMP-style validation
  • Experience scaling a fleet of deployed systems from a handful of units to dozens or more
  • Experience at an early-stage company, ideally through a period of rapid team growth
  • Working knowledge of firmware, embedded systems, and connected devices, enough to partner effectively with firmware and software leads

• You lead with concrete examples: you can walk through how you built a team, shipped a product, or recovered a slipping program, step by step
  • You're a coach first. You get energy from making a strong team even stronger, and you protect the culture that made it strong
  • You think in systems: how the pieces fit together, where the interfaces are, and what will need to scale
  • You're flexible and rigorous at the same time, comfortable trading off speed against rigor, and you can teach others to make those calls and feel good about them
  • You think strategically about how hardware serves the business, not just how to build it well
  • You're comfortable in an R&D environment today and excited to lead the shift to product, not impatient for a finished production line
  • You're curious about the biology and comfortable leaning on scientists and bioprocess engineers for what you don't know
  • You know when to be flexible and when to be assertive, and once a decision is made, you commit to it and bring your team along
  • You're a thoughtful coworker who cares about the company's mission and culture, and you actively seek feedback

lists.content:
• Own and continuously improve the calibration systems and processes used to characterize and validate Prolific’s illumination hardware.
  • Support the Lead Optical Engineer's optical simulation and modeling efforts, contributing measurements, analysis, and prototypes that inform system design and performance, with opportunity to grow into running simulations and owning modeling workstreams over time.
  • Develop and execute experiments to characterize light delivery within complex bioreactor geometries and operating conditions, analyzing the resulting measurements to identify trends, validate optical models, and improve understanding of system performance.
  • Collaborate closely across mechanical, electrical, firmware, data, biology, and bioprocess engineering to connect optical performance with cell culture behavior and process outcomes.
  • Contribute to projects that deepen Prolific’s understanding of the relationship between light, bioreactor environments, and biological response, helping translate those insights into improved illumination systems and new applications.

• PhD, MS with 2+ years, or BS with 4+ years of industry experience, in Optical Engineering, Optical Sciences, Photonics, Physics, Applied Physics, Mechanical Engineering, or a related technical field.
  • Strong foundation in optics, including geometric optics, radiometry, and optical measurement techniques.
  • Hands-on experience setting up, aligning, characterizing, and troubleshooting optical systems in a laboratory environment.
  • Experience developing and executing calibration procedures for illumination systems, optical components, and sensors.
  • Experience using optical measurement equipment such as spectrometers, photodiodes, power meters, cameras, or related instrumentation.
  • Experience working with light sources and optical delivery components, including LEDs, lasers, and fiber optics.
  • Proficiency with Python for instrument control, automation, data analysis, modeling, and visualization.
  • Demonstrated ability to design and execute experiments, analyze data, and communicate conclusions clearly.
  • Experience debugging complex systems involving optical, mechanical, electrical, and software components.
  • Ability to develop clear, reproducible documentation for calibration methods, experimental procedures, results, and technical findings.

descriptionBody:
This is a hands-on engineering role that offers the opportunity to build deep expertise in optical systems, robotic calibration and automation, and the characterization of light interactions with biological systems.

This role will own the execution and continuous improvement of optical calibration processes for illumination systems and the characterization of hardware system optical properties and biological optical properties. You will work closely with the Lead Optical Engineer to enable optical simulations, modeling, prototyping, and experiments that inform system design and performance.

This individual will collaborate with Hardware, Data, Biology, and Bioprocess Engineering teams on projects aimed at understanding the complex relationship between light delivery methods, bioreactor conditions, and cell culture performance. The work will span laboratory experimentation, optical characterization, data analysis, simulation, and system development, helping translate fundamental insights into reliable engineering solutions. Over time, this role will develop increasing ownership of optical subsystems and technical projects that ultimately enable faster and cheaper therapeutics manufacturing and expand the range of applications made possible by Prolific’s illumination technology.

Success in this position requires strong systems thinking and comfort operating both as a scientist and as an engineer. The ideal candidate enjoys working in person, operating close to real-world systems, and is comfortable applying and developing skills to pioneer solutions in an area where academic research is sparse.

This role will be primarily based on-site in Emeryville, CA.

• Conduct experiments independently, collect and analyze data in a timely manner, and maintain detailed documentation in electronic lab notebooks.
  • Conduct experiments at the Automation/CLD interface and establish efficient automation workflows (Tecan or Hamilton) for CLD processes during seed train, production, or screening (Ambr or Beacon) processes.
  • Communicate successfully with any team, demonstrating the ability to compile and present across different teams and forums within the company. 
  • Quickly analyze and provide critical data and figures to support presentations, patent applications, or publications.
  • Collaborate closely with members of the CLD team as well as other teams within Prolific Machines. Contribute to lab maintenance and safety as a good lab citizen.

Qualifications:

  • Education & Experience: A Bachelor's degree with 2-5+ years of relevant industry experience or a Master's degree with 1-4+ years of relevant experience is expected for an RA II position. Additional experience and increased independence expected at the Sr. RA level.
  • Designing and Executing Experiments: Developing and proposing experimental plans, conducting experiments, and troubleshooting analytical techniques and methodologies
  • Work Style: The candidate is expected to precisely follow protocols, design and execute experiments independently, and manage multiple tasks in a fast-paced setting.
  • Communication Skills: Strong written and verbal communication skills are essential for documenting findings and effective collaboration. Familiarity with Microsoft Office (Word, Excel, PowerPoint) or Google Workspace (Docs, Sheets, Slides) software and ability to perform independent data analysis and generating meaningful conclusions is required.

    • Technical Experience:

  • Experience with cell line development workflows (pool generation, clonal isolation, stability testing).
  • Experience with automation systems used during CLD processes (scripting experience on the Tecan or Hamilton would be an added plus).
  • Exposure to high-throughput screening platforms (e.g., Beacon, Ambr, Octet, Cedex, and other regularly used Automation systems). 
  • Experience with molecular cloning and molecular biology techniques (PCR, protein quantification).
  • Working knowledge of statistical analysis or design of experiments (DoE). Comfort working in a dynamic, fast-paced R&D environment.
  • (Nice to have) Familiarity with optogenetic systems, inducible promoters, or light-responsive protein engineering.

A successful candidate for this role will:
  • Have a flexible and independent working attitude.
  • Adapt successfully to changing situations and environments.
  • Have a strong eagerness to learn.
  • Have well-developed communication, teamwork, and organizational skills.
  • Be proactive and drive to optimize workflows.
    • This is an individual contributor role within the Research Associate track. The position is best suited for candidates who excel in hands-on execution, instrumentation, and technical operations in a laboratory setting. Growth opportunities within this role are focused on deepening technical expertise, expanding instrument proficiency, and taking on increasing operational responsibility within the Cell Line Development function.

This is a foundational, hands-on senior or staff engineering role responsible for deploying, commissioning, and supporting Prolific's systems in real-world operating environments. You will own major field deployments from planning and site preparation through installation, system integration, commissioning, validation, and handoff to customers and internal teams.

As a Field Deployment Engineer, you will operate at the intersection of mechanical, electrical, optical, software, controls, data, biology, and bioprocess engineering. You will troubleshoot complex system-level problems, work closely with cross-functional engineering teams, and translate lessons learned in the field into improvements to system design, reliability, and deployment processes.

A key part of this role will be helping define how Prolific's hardware is deployed at scale. You will be a key collaborator in developing our field deployment strategy, including site requirements, shipping, documentation creation, creating and maintaining records systems,  commissioning processes, tooling, serviceability, acceptance criteria, and operational workflows. Your experience in the field will directly inform how future generations of Prolific's hardware are designed, deployed, and supported.

Another key aspect of the role is being a master troubleshooter in high demand scenarios. You will be asked to perform a wide range of troubleshooting tasks, oftentimes in time critical situations with limited, remote-only support from subject matter experts. 

The ideal candidate enjoys working close to real-world systems, is comfortable operating hands-on in labs as well as biomanufacturing facilities, and thrives when solving new technical problems where the correct approach is not always obvious.

This role will be primarily based on-site in Emeryville, CA, with regular travel to customer and deployment sites.

lists.content:
• Lead hands-on installation, integration, startup, and commissioning of alpha, beta, and deployed systems.
  • Troubleshoot and quickly fix complex system-level issues across optical, mechanical, electrical, software, controls, using experiments, diagnostics, and historical data. Often in time-critical situations, with remote-only support from SMEs, in new configurations or environments, and with limited reference documentation.
  • Own major deployments from site readiness and planning through commissioning, handoff, and ongoing support.
  • Develop deployment plans, site requirements, commissioning procedures, system tests, and acceptance criteria.
  • Work directly with customers and partners during deployment, including technical training, scheduled maintenance, and troubleshooting.
  • Serve as a key technical collaborator in defining Prolific's hardware field deployment strategy, using field experience to inform system architecture, installation, serviceability, and operational workflows.
  • Own and improve deployment documentation, including facilities checklists, training materials, SOPs, and field procedures.
  • Partner cross-functionally to identify root causes, resolve field issues, and translate deployment learnings into product and process improvements.
  • Develop tools and processes that improve deployment reliability, repeatability, efficiency, and scalability.
  • Perform engineering upgrades to field deployed equipment, owning the end-to-end process.
  • Mentor junior engineers and field technicians in systems integration, commissioning, troubleshooting, and field engineering practices.
  • Perform test engineering functions (developing, executing, documenting, and improving tests) on deployable and prototype systems and subsystems.

• BS or MS with 5+ years of relevant engineering experience, or equivalent experience owning the deployment of complex engineering systems required for the Sr. Engineer level. Additional experience expected at the Staff Engineer level.
  • Experience deploying, commissioning, integrating, and supporting prototype systems in laboratory, manufacturing, or customer environments.
  • Experience transitioning R&D systems into manufacturing or production environments.
  • A customer-focused mindset with a proven track record of achieving internal as well as external project success with delighted customers.
  • Strong systems engineering mindset with the ability to troubleshoot interactions across mechanical, electrical, optical, software, controls, and process systems.
  • Experience independently leading technical projects or engineering workstreams, including commissioning, validation, acceptance testing, or qualification.
  • Strong experimental and analytical skills, with the ability to design tests, analyze data, isolate failure modes, and develop practical engineering solutions.
  • Experience with sensors, instrumentation, data acquisition, and automated test equipment; ability to read mechanical drawings, electrical schematics, and system documentation.
  • Strong technical communication and documentation skills, with experience working directly with customer engineering, facilities, manufacturing, or operations teams.
  • Willingness to travel regularly to customer and deployment sites (domestic and international) and work hands-on with hardware in a dynamic startup environment. Travel estimated to be 30-40%.

• Experience deploying laboratory automation, bioprocessing equipment, manufacturing systems, robotics, optical systems, or complex scientific instrumentation.

  • Experience with industrial controls, PLCs, motion systems, robotics, or automation.
  • Experience with commissioning and qualification in regulated or highly controlled environments.

  • Excited to help shape how Prolific's hardware is deployed and supported as the company scales.

descriptionBody:
This is a foundational, hands-on senior or staff engineering role responsible for deploying, commissioning, and supporting Prolific's systems in real-world operating environments. You will own major field deployments from planning and site preparation through installation, system integration, commissioning, validation, and handoff to customers and internal teams.

As a Field Deployment Engineer, you will operate at the intersection of mechanical, electrical, optical, software, controls, data, biology, and bioprocess engineering. You will troubleshoot complex system-level problems, work closely with cross-functional engineering teams, and translate lessons learned in the field into improvements to system design, reliability, and deployment processes.

A key part of this role will be helping define how Prolific's hardware is deployed at scale. You will be a key collaborator in developing our field deployment strategy, including site requirements, shipping, documentation creation, creating and maintaining records systems,  commissioning processes, tooling, serviceability, acceptance criteria, and operational workflows. Your experience in the field will directly inform how future generations of Prolific's hardware are designed, deployed, and supported.

Another key aspect of the role is being a master troubleshooter in high demand scenarios. You will be asked to perform a wide range of troubleshooting tasks, oftentimes in time critical situations with limited, remote-only support from subject matter experts. 

The ideal candidate enjoys working close to real-world systems, is comfortable operating hands-on in labs as well as biomanufacturing facilities, and thrives when solving new technical problems where the correct approach is not always obvious.

This role will be primarily based on-site in Emeryville, CA, with regular travel to customer and deployment sites.
descriptionBodyPlain:
This is a hands-on engineering role that offers the opportunity to build deep expertise in optical systems, robotic calibration and automation, and the characterization of light interactions with biological systems.
This role will own the execution and continuous improvement of optical calibration processes for illumination systems and the characterization of hardware system optical properties and biological optical properties. You will work closely with the Lead Optical Engineer to enable optical simulations, modeling, prototyping, and experiments that inform system design and performance.
This individual will collaborate with Hardware, Data, Biology, and Bioprocess Engineering teams on projects aimed at understanding the complex relationship between light delivery methods, bioreactor conditions, and cell culture performance. The work will span laboratory experimentation, optical characterization, data analysis, simulation, and system development, helping translate fundamental insights into reliable engineering solutions. Over time, this role will develop increasing ownership of optical subsystems and technical projects that ultimately enable faster and cheaper therapeutics manufacturing and expand the range of applications made possible by Prolific’s illumination technology.
Success in this position requires strong systems thinking and comfort operating both as a scientist and as an engineer. The ideal candidate enjoys working in person, operating close to real-world systems, and is comfortable applying and developing skills to pioneer solutions in an area where academic research is sparse.
This role will be primarily based on-site in Emeryville, CA.

description:
Prolific Machines is ushering in a new era of biotechnology with light. Our first-of-its-kind optogenetic platform delivers unprecedented control, precisely guiding cellular behavior when and where it matters most. Unlike existing tools used to control biology, our technology enables dynamic, tunable control over virtually any cellular function in any cell type. We're enabling partners to unlock robust efficiency, quality, and reproducibility advantages across the most complex pharmaceuticals and therapeutic proteins. Prolific is supported by leading investors, including Bill Gates’s Breakthrough Energy Ventures, Mayfield and SOSV.


The Analytical Chemistry team is looking for a Senior Scientist who will execute and improve the efficiency of core analytical procedures including titer determination and product quality assessment (Aggregation, charge heterogeneity, glycan composition).  Additionally this scientist will design and execute characterizations supporting cell line development and bioprocess development programs. This position will balance hands-on lab work, coordinating resourcing within the team and people management.

lists.content:
• Manage day to day execution of core platform assays (e.g., Protein A titer, SEC, CE-SDS, icIEF, intact/subunit mass, released glycans) for CLD and BPD programs, delivering data on agreed turnaround with consistent, documented quality.
  • Manage and coordinate research associates across multiple projects.  Translate results into recommendations for clone selection and process decisions.
  • Find and remove bottlenecks across the workflows, from sample intake and preparation through instrument time, data processing, and review. 
  • Own system suitability criteria, control standards, and performance trending for our highest volume characterizations. Lead troubleshooting and root-cause work as assay drift is observed.
  • Design, run, and interpret characterization studies (e.g., size and charge variants, PTMs, glycosylation, intact and subunit mass, peptide mapping, assembly of multispecific formats). 
  • Write and maintain clear methods, SOPs, processing templates and reports ensuring data consistency across analysts. 
  • Manage and maintain analytical instrumentation (HPLC/UPLC, CE, LC-MS including Agilent QTOF, AKTA) through preventative maintenance, calibration, coordination with instrument vendors.
  • Train and mentor Research Associates and Scientists on assay execution and characterization, and set clear standards for execution, documentation, and reporting.

• Hold a PhD in Analytical Chemistry, Biochemistry, Chemistry, Pharmaceutical Sciences, or a related field with 5+ years of biologics industry experience, or an MS/BS with equivalent relevant industry experience.
  • Have a track record of measurably improving the throughput, turnaround, or robustness of analytical workflows in a high-volume setting.
  • Have deep hands-on expertise in chromatographic and electrophoretic methods for biologics (e.g., Protein A, SEC, RP, IEX; CE-SDS, icIEF), including troubleshooting.
  • Have hands-on LC-MS experience for protein characterization (intact and subunit mass, peptide mapping, PTM and glycan analysis) and with MS data processing software.
  • Have led the characterization of a biologic for a project team: designing studies, interpreting complex or conflicting data, and making a clear recommendation.
  • Bring statistical thinking to experimental design and interpretation. 
  • Have effectively managed research associates and early career scientists. 
  • Are highly organized, can balance routine delivery with project work, and make trade-offs explicit rather than absorbing them.
  • Have strong communication skills and are comfortable presenting at multiple levels of technical detail.
  • Experience with complex modalities (e.g., bispecifics, fusion proteins) and CHO-based expression and process development is a plus. 
  • Familiarity with phase-appropriate method qualification (ICH Q2(R2)/Q14) and IND-enabling CMC analytics, as our programs advance toward the clinic is a plus.
